summary: Mexico City is a vibrant mega-metropolis blending pre-Columbian history, Spanish colonial architecture, and cutting-edge contemporary culture. World-class museums, legendary street food, and iconic neighborhoods like Coyoacán and Roma make it one of North America's most dynamic destinations. The city's high altitude offers comfortable temperatures year-round and stunning photographic opportunities at every turn.

activities.name: Templo Mayor Archaeological Site
activities.description: Explore the ruins of the great Aztec temple complex at the heart of Tenochtitlan, with excellent on-site museum detailing Mexica civilization.

activities.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
activities.description: One of the world's finest anthropological museums, home to the iconic Aztec Sun Stone and extensive pre-Hispanic artifacts.

activities.name: Xochimilco Floating Gardens
activities.description: Take a traditional boat tour through the UNESCO-listed canals and gardens of Xochimilco, a tranquil escape with indigenous heritage.

activities.name: Coyoacán Historic Neighborhood Walking Tour
activities.description: Wander cobblestone streets, visit Frida Kahlo's Blue House museum, explore bohemian plazas and colonial architecture in this charming neighborhood.

activities.name: Palacio Nacional and Murals
activities.description: View Diego Rivera's magnificent murals depicting Mexican history in this government building next to the Zócalo, free to explore.

activities.name: La Alameda Central Park
activities.description: Stroll through Mexico City's historic central park, lined with monuments, museums, and street performers in the heart of downtown.

activities.name: Street Food and Market Tour
activities.description: Guided food tour through markets and street stalls sampling tacos, tamales, elotes, and regional specialties with local experts.

activities.name: Belleza Mexicana Night Out in Polanco
activities.description: Experience Mexico City's premier nightlife district with rooftop bars, clubs, and lounges in the upscale Polanco neighborhood.

activities.name: Teotihuacán Day Trip
activities.description: Visit the magnificent pre-Columbian pyramids north of Mexico City, climbing the Pyramid of the Sun for panoramic views.

activities.name: Bosque de Chapultepec Forest and Castle
activities.description: Explore Mexico City's largest park containing museums, the historic Chapultepec Castle, and peaceful woodland trails.

activities.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul)
activities.description: Visit the iconic blue house where artist Frida Kahlo lived and worked, now a museum showcasing her art and personal belongings.

activities.name: Barrio Antiguo and Garibaldi Plaza
activities.description: Experience traditional Mexican music and culture at Garibaldi Plaza, surrounded by historic colonial architecture and mariachi bands.

spots.name: Floating Gardens of Xochimilco

spots.name: Coyoacán's Plaza Hidalgo

photography.goldenHourNotes: Mexico City's high altitude (2,250m) creates exceptionally clear golden hours with vibrant colors lasting longer than sea-level cities. Early mornings often feature dramatic mist in Xochimilco and surrounding areas, while evening light bathes colonial architecture in warm tones. The city's dense urban environment provides endless compositional opportunities with dramatic contrasts between shadows and illuminated facades.

weather.seasonality: Mexico City has a mild climate year-round due to high altitude, with cool dry winters (December-March) and warm wet summers (May-September). The best time to visit is November through April when skies are clear, temperatures pleasant, and rainfall minimal.
weather.summary: Mexico City's 2,250-meter elevation creates spring-like conditions throughout the year with temperatures rarely exceeding 25°C. Rainy season (May-September) brings afternoon showers but dramatic cloud formations, while dry season offers clear skies perfect for photography and sightseeing.

hotels.name: Presidente Intercontinental Mexico City
